statement:
Given that
$$\int_0^1 (ax+b)\,dx = 1$$
and
$$\int_0^1 x(ax+b)\,dx = 1,$$
find the value of $a+b$.
solution:
Compute the first integral:
$$\int_0^1 (ax+b)\,dx = \left[\tfrac12 ax^2+bx\right]_0^1 = \tfrac12 a+b = 1.$$
Multiplying by 2:
$$a+2b=2. \tag{1}$$

Compute the second integral:
$$\int_0^1 x(ax+b)\,dx = \int_0^1 (ax^2+bx)\,dx = \left[\tfrac13 ax^3+\tfrac12 bx^2\right]_0^1 = \tfrac13 a+\tfrac12 b = 1.$$
Multiplying by 6:
$$2a+3b=6. \tag{2}$$

Subtract $2\times$(1) from (2):
$$(2a+3b)-2(a+2b)=6-4 \quad\Rightarrow\quad -b=2 \quad\Rightarrow\quad b=-2.$$

Substitute into (1): $a+2(-2)=2$, so $a=6$.

Therefore
$$a+b=6+(-2)=4,$$
which is **option F**.

(Check: $\int_0^1(6x-2)dx=[3x^2-2x]_0^1=1$ ✓, and $\int_0^1 x(6x-2)dx=[2x^3-x^2]_0^1=1$ ✓.)
hints: Evaluate both integrals to get two linear equations in a and b.
Solve the simultaneous equations for a and b.
